text:
alyssa: Quick thread — I think our current dedicated-pool autoscale is conflating two problems. Proposal: split into a bounded fastpath for immediate admission/prewarm and a planner that runs predictive & cost-aware scaling. Thoughts?
kevin: Sounds promising. What do you mean by 'bounded' for fastpath?
alyssa: Fastpath should make constant-time decisions: admit, reject, or steal from burst credits. No heavy forecasting. It only uses local pool state + cheap signals (inflight, token-rate). Planner does the heavier lookahead and vends reservations.
sam: How do we avoid thrash between fastpath and planner if planner is slower to react?
alyssa: Two levers: (1) soft headroom that fastpath maintains (ms-level), (2) planner issues reserved tokens/leases with TTLs and can escalate prewarm when cost model says so. Also add hysteresis and a decay window for planner-driven changes.
jordan: Operator surface changes? We need backward compatibility for dedicated pool configs and the operator API.
alyssa: Minimal change: introduce `scaling_regime` block in pool spec. Default maps to existing behavior. Example config below.
kevin: can you paste the example?
alyssa: ```
scaling_regime:
  fastpath:
    max_burst: 6
    headroom_ms: 150
    token_rate_limit: 2500
  planner:
    lookahead_s: 45
    cost_weight: 0.7
    reserve_ttl_s: 300
```
marie: Metrics to validate: P99 tail latency, prewarm hit rate, # of planner-triggered scale-ups, and oscillation events (back-to-back up/down within window). Also cost per token.
kevin: Nice. Can orch-bot run a synthetic sim with our last 7 days QPS to see oscillation patterns?
orch-bot: scheduled sim job `sim-8342109999` for pool alpha with 7d trace. ETA 18m. Will post results + heatmap. :robot_face:
sam: I'll take the canary rollout after sim. Plan: run sim, tweak `headroom_ms` and `lookahead_s`, then canary on pool `alpha` (10% traffic). I'll own metrics dashboard.
alyssa: Perfect. Can we also add a cheap admission probe: a single `is_fastpath_compatible()` call in the runtime so we don't regress latency on critical path? If yes, we keep fastpath O(1).
jordan: Agree. Also suggest a short runbook step: if oscillation > X, automatically back off planner aggressiveness.
marie: +1 on runbook. I'll add SLO checks and alert thresholds.
kevin: :thumbsup: good plan.
alyssa: thanks — will follow up with a short RFC summary and the config CRD patch.
